subject: IR evidence exchange & temporary access clarifications
messages:
From: Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@clearstream.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: ClearStream Security <security@clearstream.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: incident response artifacts & short-term access for SOC2 review

Hi Jordan,

We’re preparing for a SOC 2 evidence collection window next week and need to get a handful of incident-response artifacts and short-term access to support our audit team. Can Redwood provide the following by EOD 2026-12-03?

- Current Incident Response Plan (redacted if needed)
- Runbooks for detection/containment for auth anomalies
- Forensic log manifest (list of log sources + sample retention slices)
- A small batch of sanitized telemetry / sample logs (redacted PII) covering Aug–Oct 2026
- Temporary, time-limited access (S3 or signed share) for two members of our audit team (names below)

Audit contacts who will need access:
- Daniel Perez <daniel.perez@clearstream.com>
- Mei Wong <mei.wong@clearstream.com>

Redaction constraints: we cannot accept raw customer PII or full IP-address tables. If you can provide hashed identifiers and an index mapping (redacted) that will meet our compliance requirements. Please also include chain-of-custody notes for any artifacts.

If you need a formal request on ClearStream letterhead let me know; otherwise this email will suffice to start the exchange.

Attached: sso_audit_questions.xlsx (list of fields auditors prioritize).

Thanks — we appreciate the quick turnaround.

— Alice
Alice Thompson
Security Program Manager, ClearStream
security@clearstream.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@clearstream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: incident response artifacts & short-term access for SOC2 review

Alice — thanks for the clear ask. We can support this and I’m looping in Marissa (Head, Security Ops) and Naomi (Customer Success lead) to coordinate delivery and access. Proposed immediate plan: 

1) Marissa will prepare a redacted IRP and runbooks + forensic log manifest and post those to a secured Drive folder.
2) For sanitized telemetry / sample logs we’ll produce scoped extracts (hashing/PII redaction) and include a manifest that documents redaction rules.
3) Access method: presigned S3 URLs with 7-day expiry + per-file audit logging OR a temporary, limited-access share account with read-only keys. We’ll include an audit trail.
4) Mutual action plan: I’ll send a short MAP with milestones (artifact delivery, access grant, confirmation call).

Attachments: mutual_action_plan_draft.docx; access_sla_matrix.csv (draft SLA for access duration/renewal).

Marissa / Naomi — can you confirm artifacts, attach the first deliverables, and call out any redaction caveats? Alice — if the presigned-link approach works we’ll provision for Daniel and Mei and send the access steps once they accept the access agreement (DocuSign link below).

DocuSign (access agreement): https://app.docusign.com/XYZ-templates/clearstream-access-agreement

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
<signature removed>
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@clearstream.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T15:27:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: incident response artifacts & short-term access for SOC2 review

Jordan / Alice — thanks. Confirming Redwood can deliver the requested material. Deliverables we will upload to the secured folder by 2026-12-02: 

- redacted_irp_v2.pdf (IR plan with sensitive customer references redacted; control owners preserved) — attachment included
- runbooks_auth_anomaly.md (detection + containment runbook; internal-only notes removed)
- forensic_log_manifest.txt (list of log sources, retention windows, sampling slices) — attachment included
- telemetry_samples.tar.gz (sanitized samples; filenames and a short readme with redaction algorithm details)
- access_sla_matrix.csv (how long links last and renewal flow) — attachment included

Access approach (summary):
- We will use presigned S3 URLs scoped per-file, expiry = 7 days by default.
- Each link will be single-download and require the recipient to verify via the DocuSign access agreement we shared.
- If ClearStream needs an extension we can issue a one-time 72-hour extension on request; extensions require an internal approval ticket and will be logged.
- All downloads will be logged to our audit pipeline; we’ll include a download manifest for chain-of-custody.

Redaction notes:
- IPs will be pseudonymized (SHA-256) in the samples.
- User identifiers (emails, account ids) will be hashed and an aggregate mapping (counts per hashed id) provided where useful.
- We will not include unredacted customer PII. Any request for additional granularity will require a short justification and an approval from our security team.

Attachments included in this message: redacted_irp_v2.pdf; forensic_log_manifest.txt; access_sla_matrix.csv

If that timeline works I’ll upload the folder and send DocuSign invites to Daniel and Mei. Jordan / Naomi — please confirm who will be the primary point of contact for the verification call after delivery.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head, Security Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0123
From: Alice Thompson <alice.thompson@clearstream.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: incident response artifacts & short-term access for SOC2 review

Thanks Marissa — that all looks good and the 7-day presigned link approach is acceptable. A couple of small clarifications before you publish: 

1) Can the one-time 72-hour extension be requested by the ClearStream audit lead (Daniel) directly, or does it need to come through our legal/compliance team?
2) For the pseudonymized IPs: will the logs include the original port and timestamp granularity our auditors ask for (timestamps at second-level resolution)? They don’t need raw IPs, just the ability to correlate events by hashed IP + exact timestamp.

If those answers are yes we’ll sign the DocuSign and Daniel will accept the access invite.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Alice
